## 6. Actions {#actions}

### Buttons

Four kinds. All are weight 500 and show the focus outline on `:focus-visible`.

| Kind | Rest | Hover | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main | the accent tint: `text-accent-strong`, `bg-accent-subtle`, `border-accent-subtle` | `bg-accent-subtle-hover`, `border-accent` | at most one per view |
| Secondary | `bg-surface`, `border-default`, `text-default` | `bg-hover`, `border-strong` | everything else with a frame |
| Quiet | text only, `text-muted`, 8px side padding | `bg-hover`, `text-default` | low-weight actions; replaces the grey-400 text links |
| Destructive | `text-danger`, `border-danger` at 6% fill, `border-danger-subtle` | `border-danger` at 12% fill, `border-danger` | only to confirm a removal |
| Disabled | `text-disabled`, transparent, `border-default` | none | |

The classes are `.blockr-btn` with a kind, `.blockr-btn--main`,
`--secondary`, `--quiet` or `--danger`, and a size, `.blockr-btn--m`, `--s` or
`--xs` (`blockr-buttons.css`); a bare `.blockr-btn` is a secondary m.

There is no solid accent button. `blockr-theme.css` maps Bootstrap's button
classes onto the kinds: `btn-primary` is main; `btn-default`,
`btn-secondary`, `btn-outline-secondary` and `btn-light` are secondary;
`btn-link` is quiet; `btn-danger` is destructive; `.btn` takes size m and
`btn-sm` size s. Shiny's `actionButton()` and `downloadButton()` follow this
section through it. The mapping also restyles the buttons of Shiny's own
modals, which is intended. `btn-success` has no kind and goes.

| Size | Height | Text | Side padding | Radius | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| m | 42px | 14px | 16px | 8px | beside inputs |
| s | 30px | 13px | 11px | 6px | toolbars, dialogs |
| xs | 26px | 12px | 9px | 4px | a header strip, next to the gear |

The crossfilter reset, the patient-profile drill reset and the ↵ button of
a text field are instances of the main style. The two resets take these
sizes; the ↵ button keeps the field's 24px (see [Text and number
fields](#text-and-number-fields)), since it sits inside a 42px field.

### Icon buttons (tools)

Header tools (search, download, the builder/code switch) are 26px, radius 4,
bare, icon `text-muted`. Hover: `bg-hover`, icon `text-default`. Every
icon-only button has a tooltip. Tools do not shrink with the panel.

The dock header has the "…" menu, and next to it a block's own control where
the block has one (the AI assistant's sparkle, at every width, until a global
assistant replaces it). They look like the tools above: the title's size and
weight make the header read as the block's name, and a quieter icon would
fall under the 3:1 an active control needs (WCAG 1.4.11), as `text-disabled`
(2.5:1) and `border-strong` (1.5:1) do on white.
The preview's eye stays in the header
too, left of the block's own control: while building, the preview is what
gets switched most. Controls is the menu's first row, with its familiar icon
and a check when on, then a rule, then the block's actions. The header has one size at every
card width, or the compact one when the board asks for it. The accent tint's fill and frame are for the builder/code
switch, which changes how a value is edited rather than what is shown.

### The gear button

- 26px, radius 4, 1px `border-default`, the one framed square in the header
  row. Icon: Bootstrap `gear-fill` at 14px, `text-muted`.
- Hover: `text-default`, `border-strong`, `bg-hover`.
- While the tray is open: the accent tint.
- One class, `.blockr-gear-btn`, on every gear and on nothing else. Tooltip
  "Settings".
- No gear when a block has no options, including per mode.

### Small icons

Drag handles, remove buttons and fold arrows are drawn with thin strokes and
small dots in `text-muted`. Handles and remove buttons are hidden at rest and
appear on hover or keyboard focus of their row; remove turns `text-danger` on
hover. Fold arrows stay visible. The crossfilter's filter cards are the
exception (see [Special blocks](#special)).

The icons are blockr.ui's, one SVG file each, read two ways: `Blockr.icons`
in JavaScript and `small_icon()` in R. A package draws them from there rather
than keeping a copy of the SVG, and rather than from Font Awesome through
`shiny::icon()`, which loads two stylesheets of about 2,400 rules (26 KB
compressed) and a 156 KB font for one glyph.

### Chevrons

One chevron does every disclosure, dropdown and "go to" arrow:
`Blockr.icons.chevron` in blockr.ui, `small_icon("chevron")` in R. It is a
12px box with the path `M3 4.5l3 3 3-3`, half the box wide and a quarter
high with a right angle at the tip, stroked at 1.4px with round caps and
joins and no fill.

- Size: 12px; 10px inside a 24px pill or a bare select in a row. The stroke
  stays 1.4px at both sizes.
- Colour: `text-muted` at rest; `text-default` on hover of the chevron or of
  the row or control it belongs to; `text-disabled` when disabled.
- A fold (something opens in place: a table section, an outline chapter, a
  settings section) points down when open and right when closed, rotating
  −90°.
- A menu or select (something floats: Select, a pill, the navbar's view menu,
  a split button) points down and flips up (180°) while its menu is open.
- A "go to" arrow (an options page, back, the next page of rows) points right
  or left and does not rotate.
- Every rotation uses `--blockr-transition`.
- No other glyph does this job: no Bootstrap Icons chevrons, no Bootstrap's
  own select and accordion arrows, no border triangles, no ▾ ▸ ‹ ›
  characters.

### Keyboard shortcuts

- **Hint only where a key does something a user would not guess.** Enter
  committing a field, ⌘↵ running code, ⌘S saving. Keys every web page has
  (Tab, the arrows, Escape closing a menu) get no hint.
- **What each key means**, everywhere:

  | Key | Means |
  |---|---|
  | ↵ | commit this one thing: a field's value, a pick in a menu, one value added to a list |
  | ⌘↵ (Ctrl+↵) | run or send, where ↵ makes a new line: Run in the code editor |
  | Esc | cancel: drop what is not committed, close what floats. Never saves. |
  | Tab, a click elsewhere | leave; a field commits when you leave it. The code field's open completion list is the exception: Tab takes the highlighted completion, as an R editor does |
  | ⇧↵ | nothing of blockr's own |

- **Notation.** Keys are glyphs: ↵ Enter, ⇧ Shift, ⌘ Command, ⌥ Option, and
  "Esc". On a Mac they run together with no "+" (⌘⇧S, ⌘↵). Elsewhere
  modifiers are words joined by "+" (Ctrl+Shift+S, Ctrl+↵). Enter is ↵ on
  both.
- **Only the form that applies**, never "⌘/Ctrl". blockr.ui decides once per
  page: `.blockr-mac` on the root, `Blockr.isMac`, `Blockr.keys("Mod+S")` in
  JavaScript and `shortcut("Mod+S")` in R, where `Mod` is Command on a Mac
  and Ctrl elsewhere. No package checks the platform itself.
- **Where the hint goes.** After the action's name, as muted meta text: the
  meta slot of a menu row ("Save ⌘S"), after a button's label ("Run ⌘↵"). It
  never replaces the name, and it is not repeated in a tooltip. The one
  exception is a text field's ↵ button, where pressing the key is the whole
  action: it shows ↵ alone and names itself "Apply (Enter)" to screen
  readers.
- **No sentences.** Where several keys need explaining, pair each key with
  its verb: "↵ add · Esc cancel".

### The navbar

The board's toolbar: 48px high, `bg-surface`, a `border-default` rule under
it, every control 30px, tokens only.

- Left: the logo, then the workflow's name, then its save state as 12px
  `text-muted` text ("Not saved", "Saved just now"), then one quiet "…"
  workflow menu (save as, copy link, history, new). No split buttons.
- The workflow's name is its ID: chosen in a dialog at the first save, unique,
  like a file name (spaces allowed). It is shown in the body face, weight 600,
  never monospace. There is no separate title.
- Right: the view menu as a quiet button (current view marked by weight 600,
  no fill), the board options gear, and the account avatar last: a 28px circle
  with the count's accent fill (`border-accent` at 14%) and a
  `text-accent-strong` initial.
- Hover on every navbar control is `bg-hover`. The spinner's label is the
  light tooltip.

Drawn in the [design system page](design-system/index.html#actions).

---

## 7. Floating layer {#floating}

blockr has no popovers. Floating things are menus (choices and actions, opened
by a click) and tooltips (names, on hover). The gear tray is in flow and not
part of this layer.

### Stacking

A z-index is one of two things, and no other number is written:

- **Inside a component** it orders siblings, from -1 to 3. It cannot reach
  past the component's own stacking context, so it needs no scale.
- **Against the page** (fixed, or portalled to `<body>`) it names a layer.
  The layers are Bootstrap's stack, which bslib puts on every page, so a
  blockr layer lands between Bootstrap's own instead of guessing past them.

| Layer | Token | Value | Bootstrap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overlay in the content (a drag ghost, a drop line) | `--blockr-z-overlay` | 1000 | `$zindex-dropdown` |
| Sticky header | `--blockr-z-sticky` | 1020 | `$zindex-sticky` |
| Fixed bar | `--blockr-z-fixed` | 1030 | `$zindex-fixed` |
| Side panel over the page | `--blockr-z-offcanvas` | 1045 | `$zindex-offcanvas` |
| Modal | `--blockr-z-modal` | 1055 | `$zindex-modal` |
| Menu | `--blockr-z-menu` | 1070 | `$zindex-popover` |
| Tooltip | `--blockr-z-tooltip` | 1080 | `$zindex-tooltip` |
| Toast | `--blockr-z-toast` | 1090 | `$zindex-toast` |

A layer sits above everything it can open from: a menu opens from a modal or a
side panel, and a tooltip names a menu's rows. The overlay layer is for something
that belongs to the content but has to be fixed on `<body>` (Shiny's output
wrappers can leave nothing to position against): it covers the content it is
dragged over and stays under the navbar and everything that floats. The tests in blockr.ui hold its
stylesheets to these two forms and the layers to Bootstrap's values.

### Dismissing

Anything that can be dismissed is a layer: a menu, a tooltip, the gear tray, a
side panel, and a field holding an edit not yet committed. Layers stack in the
order they opened. One listener on the page decides what Escape and an outside
click close; a control does not stop the event itself.

- **Escape** acts on the top layer only. A second press acts on the next one.
  Escape never commits: a dirty field reverts, a title being renamed restores,
  a menu closes and returns focus to its trigger.
- **An outside click** (outside the layer and everything opened from it)
  closes menus and tooltips, and commits a dirty field, as blur does. It
  leaves the gear tray and a pinned side panel open.
- **The gear tray** closes by its gear and by Escape. It is in the page, not
  over it, so Escape closes the tray that holds focus; several trays can be
  open at once.
- **A side panel** floats until it is pinned. Unpinned, Escape and an outside
  click close it. Pinned, it is part of the page, and only its close button
  closes it.

The stack is `Blockr.layer` (blockr-ui.js). It reads Escape and the pointer
before anything else on the page does, so a menu over a modal, or a field in a
side panel, takes the key before the modal or the panel sees it. A click is
read on pointerdown: it lands in the topmost layer it hits, a layer's trigger
counting as part of it, and closes the layers opened after that one. A tooltip
is a layer too, so while one shows, the next Escape hides it and leaves the
layer under it open.

### Menus

Every menu, dropdown and list that floats uses one surface:

- `bg-raised`, 1px `border-default`, radius 8 (`radius-lg`, the same as the
  field it opens from), `shadow-md`.
- Rows at 14px, radius 4 (`radius-sm`), 10px side padding. Meta text 13px.
- Row height and inner padding follow the kind of list, wherever it opens
  from. A list of values is scanned, so it stays dense; a menu of actions is
  mostly a short list and gets more room.

| List | Rows | Inner padding |
|---|---|---|
| a list of values (`Blockr.Select`, `Select.menu()`) | 32px | 4px |
| a menu of actions (`Blockr.menu`, `action_menu()`) | 34px | 6px |
- The dock "…" menu, the download menus, the add menu and the @ menu move to
  it. The beak belongs to the gear tray only.
- Menus of actions are `Blockr.menu` (blockr.ui): rows, gaps, dividers,
  group titles and an optional head. A menu of actions is a little airier
  than a Select list: 6px panel padding and rows 34px, at the same radius 4
  in the same radius-8 panel.
- Plain actions have no icon. A row gets one only when it is more than a
  plain action: it opens a mode or another surface ("Manage pages"), or it
  destroys something ("Remove", a bin). Such a row sits in a group of its
  own, after a gap or a divider, so a label with an icon never sits right
  under one without. The toggle for what the card shows keeps its icon too
  (Controls, the sliders).
- A destructive row is plain text at rest and turns `text-danger` on a
  `bg-danger` wash under the pointer or as the keyboard row. The current item
  (the page you are on) is weight 600 with a check at the end, no fill. Its
  classes (`.blockr-menu`, `.blockr-menu__item`, ...) also style a menu whose
  markup is rendered elsewhere, so it looks the same.

- A menu of actions (downloads, the "…" menu) is `action_menu()` or
  `Blockr.menu`: its rows run once and close it. The one remembered row is a
  toggle for what the card shows: a check at the end while on, first, in its
  own group before a divider. A menu that sets a value is
  `Blockr.Select.menu()`. The two share the surface and the placement.

**Row states.**

| State | Look |
|---|---|
| hover and keyboard row (same look) | `bg-hover`; meta text and icons turn `text-default` |
| current pick | weight 600 |
| toggle on | a check at the end, normal weight |
| multi pick | a tick (14px, `text-accent`) in a slot every row keeps; normal weight |
| disabled | listed in `text-disabled`, no hover, the reason in a tooltip |

The views menu drops its blue fill for the current view.

**Group titles and dividers.** A group title uses the section-title style
(12px, 600, uppercase, 0.05em, `text-muted`), 8px above and 4px below, inset to
the row text (10px). In a list that scrolls it is sticky. A divider (1px
`border-default`, the menu's inner padding above and below, edge to edge) separates groups without a
title, such as ordinary actions from a destructive one. A destructive item
is plain at rest, as above, and red only under the pointer or as the
keyboard row.

**Placement.** One routine for all of them (Select's `computePosition`, moved
to blockr.ui): fixed position on `body`, 4px from the trigger, flips above when
there is no room below, follows scroll, stays 8px from the viewport edge.

| Menu | Width |
|---|---|
| field dropdown | the control's width, at least 190px |
| menu from a button or a word | sized to content, 180 to 320px |

A menu lines up with the trigger's left edge, or its right edge when the
trigger is in the header row. Height up to 320px, then the list scrolls under
its sticky titles and filter box. A multi menu's tags take up to three rows and
scroll on their own past that, so the list keeps room under many picks. A
filter box (30px) appears above 8 options.
It is part of the menu, not a field: 13px, and no focus ring, since it holds
focus the whole time the menu is open.
A `Select.menu` names the role it sets in its title, because the word that
opened it names only the value.

**Content.** Long lists render up to 200 options and end with a count row that
asks you to type; server-searched lists say how many values there are. Empty
and loading rows are centred, italic, `text-muted` ("No matches", "No
options", "Loading…").

**Behaviour.** The focus stays in the filter box or on the list, and the
keyboard row is its active descendant, in a list of values and a menu of
actions alike. Arrows move the row, Enter picks, typing filters. In a menu of
actions the pointer moves the same row, Home and End jump, and Space picks
too; opened from the keyboard, the menu starts on its first row, and the down
arrow on its trigger opens it. Escape closes and returns focus to the
trigger; Tab and an outside click close. A pick closes the menu; a multi pick
keeps it open and keeps the filter text.

### The block's "…" menu

Controls (the sliders, a check when on), a divider, then Rename, Append
block, Copy block ID (the ID as mono meta text), and Remove block after a
divider, a destructive row. No head: the block's type and package are the
tooltip on its mark, and the dock header has no subtitle.

### Tooltips

One style for every name shown on hover: a small light card. `bg-raised`, 1px
`border-default`, `shadow-md`, radius 8 (`radius-lg`, as the chart's data
tooltip), 12px `text-default`, padding 5px 9px.
It shows on hover and on keyboard focus, and leaves with the pointer or focus;
Escape hides it.

- Every icon-only button and every cut-off label gets one, and so do the
  block's mark in the dock header (its type, then the package as a neutral
  badge) and every name that can be renamed in place (the gesture, see
  [Renaming in place](#renaming-in-place)). So does a segment with a terse
  label (`%`, `n`, `All`): it shows the title its caller passes. So do a
  table's sorted header (its order in words) and a link in the outline (the
  blocks it joins). Nothing else does: a button that names its action in
  full, like Save, has no tooltip.
- No native `title` tooltips remain in blockr markup: an element built in R
  carries its tooltip as `data-blockr-tooltip`, with a badge after the name
  (the mark's package) as `data-blockr-tooltip-badge`, and a control built in
  JavaScript sets it with `Blockr.tooltip.set()`. A third-party widget's
  titles are its own and stay native.
- It matches the chart's data tooltip (see [Special blocks](#special)), so
  blockr has one floating style.
- It shows after the pointer rests 300ms, and at once on keyboard focus or
  while warm (within 400ms of another card leaving, so moving along a row of
  icons does not wait at each one). It sits above the element and flips below
  only where there is no room above.
- `Blockr.tooltip` (blockr-ui.js) draws it; controls set it in place of
  `title`.

### Picking a block

- **Adding a block** is one menu at the "+", everywhere: the outline, a
  block's append, the board's Add block. Search on top, category titles, one
  row per block type with its 24px mark, its name and the package as a badge.
  Rows carry no description. The block's ID is generated, and its title is
  renamed on the block after it is added. The dock's block browser sidebar and
  its "configure before adding" step go.
- **Picking a block already on the board** (add a panel, link to, add to a
  stack) uses the same menu, listing the board's blocks: mark, title, and the
  block type as meta text. The Bootstrap modal with selectize goes.

Drawn in the [design system page](design-system/index.html#floating).

---

## 8. Labels and status {#labels}

### Four kinds, told apart by shape

| Kind | Class | Job | Shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| Badge | `.blockr-menu__badge`, `.blockr-tooltip__badge` | you only read it: "Categorical", "blockr.dplyr", "Added" | capsule |
| Tag | `.blockr-select__tag` | a value you picked, with × when it can be removed | 4px corners |
| Pill | `.blockr-pill` | a click changes a setting (the operator) | 4px corners |
| Count | none yet | a number on a button | capsule |

The word "chip" goes. Round ends mean read-only; tags, pills and buttons, which
you act on, keep 4px corners.

### Badges

- 18px capsule (`radius-pill`), 11px weight 500, 7px side padding, `bg-subtle`
  fill, 1px `border-default`, `text-muted`.
- Neutral unless it states a status or that something is on:
  - **on, added, cutting rows:** the accent tint (`bg-accent-subtle`,
    `border-accent-subtle`, `text-accent-strong`);
  - **danger, warning, success:** `bg-<status>`, `border-<status>-subtle`,
    `text-<status>`.
- Types, packages and significance levels are neutral; the type icon beside a
  name already carries the type. io's blue "info" badge becomes neutral.
- Data colours (the arm label in the cohort list, the tile's colour-by pill)
  come from the board's scale and are outside this rule.
- A count with a unit ("4 blocks") is a badge.

### Tags

24px, radius 4, 1px `border-default`, 8px side padding. Inside a field (a multi
Select, a row) a tag takes `bg-hover`, a step darker than the field, and its
name is 13px `text-default` mixed 80% with `bg-field`, so the tags do not
outshout the rest of the block. A column label after the name is 12px, the
same mix at 70%, since `text-muted` is under 4.5:1 on `bg-hover`. The
crossfilter's "Filter by" tags sit on the surface: `bg-surface`, `text-default`, and `bg-hover` while their card is open.
The × follows [Controls](#controls). The accent tint on a tag
means the value is cutting rows. The crossfilter's "Filter by" pills are tags
by this rule, and the read-only items in a drill receipt are tags without ×.

### Pills

Specified under "A pill that opens a menu" in [Controls](#controls).

### Counts

- 16px capsule, at least 16px wide, 4px side padding, 11px weight 600,
  tabular figures.
- Fill: the host control's colour at 14%. On an accent host that is
  `color-mix(in srgb, var(--blockr-color-border-accent) 14%, transparent)`
  with `text-accent-strong` text.
- Shown only when the number is above zero.
- On a secondary or destructive button the count takes that button's colour:
  `text-default` on a `bg-hover` fill, or `text-danger` on `border-danger` at
  14%. A count
  never brings a second colour into a button.
- A count never counts active filters (see [Messages](#messages)). No control
  shows a count at the moment.

### Showing that a block filters

- The control that undoes a filter says what the filter kept, never a count
  of filters: see the rule under [Messages](#messages).
- Dots are for block status only; the heatmap's filter dot goes.

### Block status

An 8px dot on the block's mark with a 2px `bg-surface` ring, one spec for dock
and the DAG (`block_status_badge()`). Its fills are meaning tokens, with no
status tokens of their own: the spec names each token next to its light
value, which a renderer that cannot read CSS (the DAG's canvas) draws with.

| State | Fill | When |
|---|---|---|
| stale | `text-muted` | the inputs changed since the block last ran |
| waiting | `border-warning`, drawn as a hollow ring (1.5px, `bg-surface` inside) | an input is not ready: nothing linked in, or the block upstream is unset, waiting or failed |
| failed | `border-danger` | the block failed |
| unset | `border-warning` | a required input is empty; the same amber as the empty field's cue |

Unset and waiting share the amber and differ by shape: the block that needs
you has the solid dot, and the blocks below it, which wait for it, have rings.
The amber replaces the off-palette `#eab308` blockr.dock's
`block_status_badge()` gave unset.

### Status line and plain text

The status line under the output is 12px `text-muted`: row counts, filter
state, timing, the drill receipt. These stay plain text, with no badge: column
types in the table preview (int, dbl), the status line and its receipt, the
filter trail printed in captions (in column labels, see below), the Big N at
the end of a column header.

### Column names and their labels

A column has a name (`AGE`) and often a label ("Age"). The board speaks in
names, an exhibit in labels.

| Where | Shows |
|---|---|
| a control that holds a column: Select options and the chosen value, tags, filter rows, crossfilter cards, gear fields, the @ menu | the name, then the label as meta text: 13px `text-muted`, 8px after the name, no separator, cut first when space runs out (12px inside a tag) |
| an exhibit: chart axes, legends and tooltips, output and summary tables, exports | the label only; an output table header shows the name in its tooltip |
| the table preview (a building surface) | the name, with the label on its own line under it, 12px `text-muted` |
| filter text printed with an exhibit: the filter trail in captions and exports | labels: "Sex = F; Age 18 to 64" |
| filter text that stays on the board: crossfilter shelf pills, drill receipts | names: "SEX = F" |

- No label, or a label equal to the name: the name alone. Never "unset",
  never the name twice.
- A menu opened from a word that prints labels (a slot in a chart's title or
  subtitle, "Colour by Actual Treatment") leads with the label and mutes the
  name, so the row reads like the word that was clicked (Select's
  `labelFirst`). The word belongs to the exhibit, which speaks in labels.
- A tooltip that shows both has the name, then the label muted, like the
  control. The "+N" overflow lists the hidden tags that way, one per line.
- An aggregate reads "Mean of Age", on a chart, in a table and in a rank
  table header.
- Code and decode pairs (PARAMCD and PARAM) follow the same rule: where one is
  picked, the code with the decode as meta ("ALB  Albumin (g/L)"); in an
  exhibit, the decode, with the code in the tooltip.
- One reader for every package: `attr(x, "label", exact = TRUE)`, returning
  one string or nothing. Without `exact`, a column with haven value labels
  returns those, and the readers that expect one string break.
- A sentence slot prints the name (`{@x}`) or the label (`{label(@x)}`), as
  its author writes it.

### Messages

- Required and empty: the amber cue on the field ([Controls](#controls)),
  never a banner.
- Syntax and validation text: `text-danger`.
- Empty and loading states in lists: centred, italic, `text-muted`.
- A panel or block with nothing to draw says so in one line of italic
  `text-muted`, 13px, where the content would be and left-aligned with it
  (`.blockr-empty`, `--panel` or `--block` for the padding). The italic marks
  the line as standing in for content. No icon, no second line. A link in it
  is a [slot](#the-sentence-and-its-slots) and stays upright. There are two
  kinds, and the words differ:
  - **Waiting:** a choice is missing (no patient picked, a required input
    unset). Say what is missing; when the place to choose it is in the
    block, a slot takes you there: "No patient selected. Search for one".
  - **Empty:** the answer is none (no records in the window, a filter that
    keeps no rows). Say what was looked for and where, so the reader can
    tell none from broken: "No medication records between D-30 and D189".
  A panel keeps its title and sentence above the line; the panel does not
  change size to hold it.
- A block that narrows what the reader sees (the crossfilter, the population
  filter, the patient profile under a drill) says so in one place on its
  header row. While nothing is filtered it is grey 12px text with the count
  ("306 patients"); while something is, the same place is the 26px main
  button with the reset icon and what the filter kept ("179 of 306
  patients"), which clears it. Count in the unit the reader thinks in: the
  subject when the block knows it, rows otherwise. When the total is
  unknown, the button says what is shown ("6 patients"). Its tooltip names
  the clauses it clears. No count of active filters: the controls that set
  them show that.
- A block that sends a filter on without narrowing its own view (a chart or
  table drill) names the clause in its status line, with Reset beside it.
- A block-level error or warning (a failed expression, dropped rows) uses the
  message style, above the output: `text-<status>` on `bg-<status>` with a
  `border-<status>-subtle` edge, 13px, radius 6. Danger for errors, the amber set for
  warnings.

Drawn in the [design system page](design-system/index.html#labels).

---

## 9. Special blocks {#special}

### Charts

- **Around the plot:** the header row, output title, sentence, caption and
  status line follow [The block](#block). Axis titles, legend titles and
  tooltips use column labels ([Labels](#labels)); blockr.ggplot's axis titles
  move from names to labels. Header tools are 26px (the chart's
  and composer's 30px tools move to 26px). The download is a tool: with one
  format it downloads, with several it opens an action menu (`action_menu()`),
  one row per format with the extension as meta.
- **On the canvas:** all text at `--blockr-mark-font-size` (11px), read by
  chart.js once per render. The gutter measurement (11px), the 14px label-row
  budget and the printed charts keep their numbers.
- **Canvas ink** is read from the tokens at render, so it follows the scheme and
  a theme's greys:

  | Canvas element | Token |
  |---|---|
  | axis and data labels | `text-muted` |
  | axis line | `border-strong` |
  | split lines | `border-default` |
  | separators, halo | `bg-surface` |
  | reference lines | `border-danger` |
  | face | the body face |

  Exports (PNG, pptx) take the light values. Retiring the "ECharts Theme" board
  option is a follow-up.
- **Facet strip:** the section-title style (12px, 600, uppercase, 0.05em,
  `text-muted`), centred over its panel. No card around the panel and no band
  behind the name; 24px between panels. Exports match.
- **Legend band:** HTML. Item text `text-muted`, like the axis labels. Its
  items take the focus outline. The 25 x 14px swatch stays.
- **Data tooltip:** the raised card (`bg-raised`, `border-default`, radius 8,
  `shadow-md`). Headline 13px weight 600 with the series swatch, which carries
  the series colour; rows 12px, labels `text-muted`, values `text-default` at
  500 with tabular figures. A split bar shows every segment of the hovered bar
  in one tip, so the swatch moves to the rows: the headline is the category,
  each row a level with its swatch and the column name ("drv 4"), and a count
  or a sum ends in a total under a hairline. Other aggregations name
  themselves under the headline ("Mean") instead of a total.
- **Slider bubble:** stays inverse (dark label), because it labels a thumb
  during a drag.
- **Data colours:** blockr.theme palettes.

### Tables

One style for the table preview and for every output table (the table block
and the composer table, which render annotated data frames).

- **Rows:** 30px, 14px text on a 20px line with 5px above and below, 12px side
  padding. No rules in the body; the hover wash (`bg-hover`) carries the eye
  along a row.
- **Header:** names 13px (`font-size-sm`), weight 600, `text-default`. A second
  line, 12px `text-muted`, holds the column label (weight 400) in the preview
  and the Big N (weight 600: bold, but lighter than the name) in an output
  table. When some columns have a label, a column without one keeps the empty
  line so every name sits level. The preview adds the type (`dbl`, 11px muted)
  below.
- **Header rule:** one unbroken 1px `border-default` rule under the whole
  header, row-label and row-number columns included. The card's rule above the
  preview and the footer rule are the same grey, so a table has one line
  weight.
- **Spanners** (a header over several columns) keep a tile: a 5% wash of the
  text colour, radius 7px at the top, 5px short of the columns at each side,
  so two spanners side by side read as two.
- **In a block card** a table runs to the card edges: it pulls itself out by
  the card's side inset (`--blockr-card-inset`, set by blockr.dock) and pads
  its first and last columns and its footer back in by as much. The rules, the
  hover wash and the scroll area reach the edges; every text keeps the card's
  alignment. Plots and diagrams stay inset.
- **Alignment:** numbers right-aligned in tabular figures, with their header
  right-aligned over them; text left. There is no centred option. A spanner is
  centred over its columns. Exports (PPTX, XLSX, HTML) take the same alignment.
- **Row labels** (the first column of an output table) in `text-default`.
  Missing values in `text-muted`: `NA` at 12px in the preview, an em dash in a
  summary table.
- **Groups** (an output table's sections, and rows with deeper-indented
  children): the heading at weight 600 with the fold chevron (see
  [Chevrons](#actions)) in the gutter left of its text; each indent level adds
  16px. Groups are set apart by space, not by a rule: a group's last row has
  7px below it and the next heading 11px above.
- **Fold all:** the chevron in the top-left header cell, in the same gutter as
  the group chevrons. A first-column title (composer's `column_header_left`)
  stays the producer's text, line breaks and weight included, beside it; only
  the chevron is the button. Without a title it reads "All". It points down
  while every group is open and right otherwise. Alt+click on a group heading
  folds or opens every group. Exports never carry it.
- **Hover and drill** (output tables with a drill): the hover previews what a
  click claims. A column header lights its column, a row label its row, a
  value the crossing (row and column at 3% of the text colour, the cell at 9%).
  A drill takes the same shape in `bg-selected` with `text-accent-strong`,
  with no accent bars; the crossing cell takes `bg-accent-subtle-hover` at
  weight 600.
- **Sorting:** the preview sorts on a header click: ascending, descending,
  missing values first (then ascending), off. A click on the name itself
  does not sort, since the name is text you can select. Ascending and
  descending put missing values last. An output table of an annotated data
  frame does not sort: its row order is its structure.
- **The sort cue:** sort bars, 12px, three bars of 1.4px that draw the values
  top to bottom: short to long for ascending, long to short for descending.
  Missing values first adds a hollow dot at the top right. The sorted column's
  cue is in `text-accent`. On hover the header takes the `bg-hover` wash and
  an unsorted column shows the ascending bars in `text-muted`, as what a click
  would do; neither shows while the pointer is on the name, which a click does
  not sort. The cue sits on the name's line: after the name, or before it on a
  right-aligned column, so the name stays over its numbers. The sorted header
  names its sort in the light tooltip ("Missing values first, then ascending")
  and carries `aria-sort`.
- **Preview footer:** the row range (12px muted) left, the pager right as 26px
  tools with the chevron pointing left and right, one `border-default` rule
  above. Row numbers are a 44px right-aligned gutter, 12px muted.

### Crossfilter

- **Header row:** the standard one. The count, which turns into Reset all
  while something is filtered, and the gear sit on the header row at the top. "Group by" is a field with a label; "Filter by" is
  a section title over the tags and cards. (The population filter, a block that
  joins two blocks in one, keeps its own layout.)
- **Reset all:** the header row's count, as a block that filters shows it
  (see [Messages](#messages)): the 26px main button with the reset icon and
  what the filters kept while something is filtered. Its tooltip names the
  clauses it undoes.
- **Filter by tags:** 13px tags. A tag whose card is open takes the hover wash
  (`bg-hover`); a tag cutting rows wears the accent tint, which wins when both
  hold.
- **Filter cards:** the column's name with its label as meta. Reset and remove
  are 26px tools, always shown; the reset is disabled while the card cuts no
  rows. Above 8 values the card has a search field
  ([Controls](#controls)).
- **The card's list** is a table and follows [Tables](#special): headers 13px
  weight 600 with the rule under each, rows 30px at 14px with 12px side
  padding, Count right-aligned with the sort bars before it, missing and empty
  values (`NA`, `(empty)`) in `text-muted` and last. It starts sorted by Count,
  largest first; a click flips the sorted column and a click on the other
  sorts it (values A to Z, Count largest first). It has no unsorted state.
  The 200px scroll area shows about 6 rows.
- **Pools:** the group's and the subgroup's are edited alike, and the
  subgroup's say so ("Subgroup pools", "Add subgroup pool"). A group's pools
  may overlap; a subgroup's may not, because tables pool only the outer
  split. While a subgroup's pools overlap, its fields take the amber cue
  (`border-warning`, `bg-warning`) and one 12px `text-warning` line names the
  levels in two columns and the way out.
- **Bars:** accent fill at `--blockr-mark-weight-supporting`, value end
  rounded by `--blockr-mark-radius`.
- **Settings:** in the gear tray.
- **"+ More filters"** opens a menu of every column, grouped by table, each
  with its type as a neutral badge. A column with a card is a multi pick (the
  tick); a click adds or removes its card.

### Code editor

The code, function and composer blocks share one CodeMirror editor.

- The editor is a large input: `bg-field` background, 13px mono.
- Syntax colours come from four local tokens:

  | Token | Points at |
  |---|---|
  | `--blockr-code-keyword` | `text-accent` |
  | `--blockr-code-string` | `text-success` |
  | `--blockr-code-number` | `text-warning` |
  | `--blockr-code-comment` | `text-muted` |

- Line numbers `text-muted`; the active line `bg-hover`; the input-line band is
  mixed from `border-accent`.
- Footer: Run and Accept all are 26px main buttons; Reject all is a 26px
  secondary button. The syntax message is `text-danger`.
- Code is 13px on every code surface; dplyr's expression input moves from
  14px.
- The green and red line backgrounds of an AI review diff are diff meaning and
  stay.

### Composer

The composer keeps its busy cue (after 300ms the body dims to 0.45 and a clock
runs under the sentence) and the "composed in" time that fades after 2s, both
in `text-muted`. Every block gets the same cue: past 300ms of computing, its output dims to
0.45 and a clock ("computing… 1.2 s") runs under it; nothing shows for a
faster run. blockr.core applies it from outside the block.

Drawn in the [design system page](design-system/index.html#special).

---

## 10. For package authors {#authors}

- [ ] Read meaning tokens only. No `--blockr-grey-*`, `--blockr-blue-*` or hex
      in a component.
- [ ] Tints via the tint tokens or `color-mix()` from a meaning token, never
      from a palette token or an rgba literal.
- [ ] Local settings are named `--blockr-<package>-*` and read only in that
      package's stylesheet.
- [ ] Text in one of three levels: default, muted, disabled (disabled only for
      disabled controls). No muted text on a hover or selected fill.
- [ ] Field labels 12px regular muted, 4px above; section titles in the one
      section-title class; no heading larger than the output title inside a
      block.
- [ ] Fields in the one grid: numbers and checkboxes small, selects and text
      large, tags and expressions full. Size steps on the panel, never the
      viewport.
- [ ] Controls by the decision table: checkbox, segmented control, Select
      (single or tags), pill with a menu, icon tiles, pressed icon button. No
      switches, radio buttons, cycle pills or shinyWidgets.
- [ ] Text and numbers commit on Enter or blur; nothing has an Apply button.
- [ ] Keyboard hints through `shortcut()` / `Blockr.keys()`: the platform's
      form only, muted after the action's name, ↵ alone on a field's button.
      No package checks for a Mac itself.
- [ ] Buttons: main (one per view), secondary, quiet, destructive, at 42, 30 or
      26px. No Bootstrap solid buttons.
- [ ] Header row: 26px tools, gear last, `.blockr-gear-btn` on the gear only.
      No gear if there are no options. Every option is in the gear.
- [ ] Chevrons: `Blockr.icons.chevron` (`small_icon("chevron")` in R) only,
      12px (10px in a pill). Folds point down open and right closed; menus
      flip up while open; "go to" arrows point right or left.
- [ ] Value pickers through `Blockr.Select` / `Select.menu()`, menus of
      actions through `Blockr.menu` or `action_menu()`, all placed by the
      shared routine. No popovers. Tooltips only where the Tooltips section
      gives one, using the light card; no native `title`.
- [ ] Anything Escape or a click outside closes is a layer on
      `Blockr.layer`, added when it opens and removed when it closes. No
      document listeners for Escape or outside clicks, and no
      `stopPropagation()` to keep a key from what lies around it.
- [ ] Badges are capsules and neutral unless they state status or "on".
- [ ] Columns: the name with its label as meta where a column is picked, the
      label alone in an exhibit; read labels with the shared reader.
- [ ] Focus: a field takes the accent border and the ring; everything else
      takes the focus outline, on `:focus-visible` only.
- [ ] Check the block in the dark scheme.

Drawn in the [design system page](design-system/index.html#authors).

---

## Appendix {#appendix}

### Where the code lives

Package blockr.ui owns the tokens (`inst/assets/css/blockr-tokens.css`,
`blockr-tokens-dark.css`), the block category colours and the logo's green
among them, and the shared components: the params grid (moving from
blockr.extra), `Blockr.Select` and its placement routine, `Blockr.checkbox`,
the badge, tag and pill styles, the slot and offer rules (today declared
twice, in blockr.viz `chart.css` and blockr.dm `crossfilter-block.css`), the
gear button, the tool button and the action menu (`tool_button()`,
`action_menu()`), the button classes (`.blockr-btn`), the gear tray for
blocks rendered in R (`gear_tray()`), the small icons
(`Blockr.icons`, `small_icon()` in R), the block's mark (`block_mark()`,
`block_mark_svg()`), and the column-label reader. Package blockr.dock owns
the dock header, the "…" menu, the block status dot and its spec
(`block_status_badge()`, which the DAG draws from too) and the rule that
hides the gear in simplified mode. Package blockr.theme owns data colours.

The token tests in blockr.ui check that the vocabulary changes only
deliberately, that every name follows the grammar or is a legacy alias, that
the controls read meaning tokens only, that icons, status borders and the logo
clear 3:1 on the surface in both schemes, and that consumers' fallbacks agree
with the tokens. Palette and legacy reads elsewhere in blockr.ui change only
deliberately too. To do: warn on every palette or legacy read in the packages
that consume the tokens.

### Legacy token aliases

Old names stay in `blockr-tokens.css` for a release and each keeps its old
value. Packages move over when convenient; the alias goes when nothing reads
it.

| Old name | Points at |
|---|---|
| `--blockr-color-text-primary` | `color-text-default` |
| `--blockr-color-text-secondary` | grey-700 (by job: labels and status lines go to `text-muted`; headings, content and hover states to `text-default`) |
| `--blockr-color-text-subtle` | grey-400 (by job: placeholders, meta and icons go to `text-muted`; disabled controls to `text-disabled`; a border to `border-strong`) |
| `--blockr-color-text-meta` | `color-text-muted` |
| `--blockr-color-border` | `color-border-default` |
| `--blockr-color-border-hover` | `color-border-strong` |
| `--blockr-color-bg-input` | `color-bg-field` |
| `--blockr-color-primary` | `color-bg-accent` |
| `--blockr-color-primary-hover` | `color-bg-accent-hover` |
| `--blockr-color-primary-bg` | accent-50 (keeps its old value; the accent tint `color-bg-accent-subtle` is a 7% mix, nearly the same colour) |
| `--blockr-color-error`, `--blockr-color-danger` | `color-border-danger` |
| `--blockr-color-success` | `color-border-success` |
| `--blockr-color-warning` | `color-border-warning` |
| `--blockr-color-warning-bg` | `color-bg-warning` |
| `--blockr-color-warning-text` | `color-text-warning` |
| `--blockr-font-size-section` | `font-size-lg` |
| `--blockr-font-size-title` | `font-size-xl` |
| `--blockr-shadow` | `shadow-sm` |
| `--blockr-shadow-dropdown` | `shadow-md` |

One new token reuses an old name: `--blockr-color-bg-hover` was grey-100, and
it stays grey-100 in light until the fallbacks that write `#f3f4f6` move to the
text wash. The dark scheme uses the wash already.

Removed from the UI tokens: `--blockr-color-negative` (data colour, belongs in
blockr.theme). Local names move under their owner: dock's `spinner-delay`,
`sidebar-*`, `stack-height` and header settings to `--blockr-dock-*`; viz's
`rank-*` to `--blockr-viz-rank-*`. blockr.outline drops its own `--md-*`
variables and reads the blockr tokens.

### Not specified yet

Dialogs (surface, width, title, button order), dock tabs beyond their selected
state, the DAG view, notifications (Shiny's `showNotification`), and the icon
set with its sizes (the chevron is specified under [Actions](#actions)).

### Decision record

The reasoning behind each rule, the options that were compared and the
questions they answered were in `naming.md`, `questions.html` and `topics/`
in `dev/design-system/`. They were removed once this document was complete; git
history has them (`git log --all -- dev/design-system/naming.md`).
